subject: Nonstationary Matérn correlation (and not covariance) models

messages.author: b91e54f3020c0cfd
messages.subject: Nonstationary Matérn correlation (and not covariance) models
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if in the current version of RINLA there is a possibility to impose a constraint on nonstationary Matérn models such that marginal variances are 1.
I have tried the method implemented in inla.qinv for calculating marginal variances which seems to be fast and accurate when model dimension is not too high (say, a spatial mesh with 10.000 nodes), so INLA-based estimation should still run smoothly with additional normalization of the precision matrix if I don't miss something important ...


Thanks for help,

Thomas

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Nonstationary Matérn correlation (and not covariance) models
parts:
We are working on getting a version of the model into the package that would allow this, but it's not quite there yet.  In the meantime, the closest is probably to use these methods (depending on _why_ you need it it may either work or not...).
1) renormalise the model at a "base" model, so that for theta=c(0,...,0), say, the variance is constant. This can be done by changing the offset column in B.tau based on the inla.qinv output for an unnormalised model.
2) make sure you don't use a plain kappa& tau parameterisation, but instead one that is closer to decoupling the range and the marginal variances.  See for example the lindgren&rue 2015 Journal of Statistical Software paper for prototype code for that.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Nonstationary Matérn correlation (and not covariance) models
parts:
Step 1 will only help close to some "basic" nonstationary;  and yes, short-range nonstationarity is difficult to handle with this method, as it is based on local staetionarity assumptions.

Finn
